primitives.name: Sudden Death Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: Introduction** Prior to the 2010-2011 season, the NFL overtime rules stated that the first team to score a touchdown (TD), field goal (FG), or safety won the game whether or not both teams had received an opportunity to score.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'Team A possesses the ball', 'U': 'Team B possesses the ball', 'W_A': 'Team A wins', 'W_B': 'Team B wins'}
primitives.assumptions: Game ends upon first scoring event; no second chance for the non-scoring team.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When either team scores first, the game terminates immediately.

layer2.mapping: State transition graph where T → W_A or U → W_B represents immediate termination.

primitives.name: Modified Sudden Death Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: The new rule does not allow the initial receiving team to win with a FG on their first possession, only with a TD.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'Field goal attempt', 'TD': 'Touchdown attempt', 'S': 'Safety attempt', 'A_pos': 'Team A has possession', 'B_pos': 'Team B has possession'}
primitives.assumptions: Initial team must score TD to win; otherwise, normal overtime continues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Transition from A_pos to B_pos if no TD scored.

layer2.mapping: Conditional transition matrix where F and S do not lead to absorption unless followed by TD.
layer2.telemetry: Probability of TD vs FG/S outcomes in first possession.

primitives.name: Overtime Duration Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our analysis shows that the modified sudden death rule change increased the average overtime from 7 minutes 1 second to 7 minutes 37 seconds and that the probability of the team possessing the ball first winning decreased from 59.9% to 55.4%.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{\\text{overtime}}': 'Duration of overtime in minutes', 'P(T=t)': 'Probability of overtime lasting exactly t minutes'}
primitives.assumptions: Markovian process with fixed state transitions and finite expected duration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Expected value convergence under stationary distribution.

layer2.mapping: Expected overtime duration computed via summing time-weighted probabilities across all possible lengths.

The study employs Markov chains to model NFL overtime dynamics, distinguishing between sudden death (SD), modified sudden death (MSD), and MSD with 10-minute periods. Each rule variant defines distinct state transitions and absorbing states—winning teams or ties. The transition probabilities reflect scoring likelihoods and possession changes. For SD, transitions are binary: A_pos → W_A or B_pos → W_B. MSD modifies this by requiring TD for first-team victory, altering transition paths. The model computes expected overtime durations and win probabilities per team. These primitives form a dual framework: one for stochastic evolution (GSE) and one for probabilistic inference (GSI). Failure modes include misestimation of scoring rates or ignoring temporal dependencies. The Markov structure ensures memorylessness, simplifying computation but potentially underrepresenting strategic behavior.
